To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

postsynthetic processing is possible on a macroscopic scale for hollow tubular materials and that the postsynthetic processing can be controlled to induce an amorphization-crystallization transition and to convert the material from Cu(OH) 2 to Cu2O and finally to Cu.
we have demonstrated that postsynthetic processing can be used to produce hollow silica-supported metal-oxide and metal tubes.
we can postsynthetically process copper hydroxide-tubes into a variety of copper-based materials without compromising the tubular structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of copper hydroxides and copper oxides in the form of hollow tubes.
the postsynthetic modification of silica tubes.
postsynthetic processing of Cu hydroxide-sol-gel derived silica tubes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the postsynthetic processing of the copper hydroxide silica tubes is possible and the results are promising.
the postsynthetic processing is an effective way to produce Cu2O and CuO in a tubular morphology.
the postsynthetic treatment of Cu(OH)x/SiO2 tubes allows us to produce CuO, CuO2, Cu2O and metallic copper in the form of hollow tubular structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
postsynthetic treatment of Cu(OH)x-silica tubes can be used to control the morphology and composition of the Cu-based nanomaterials.
the Cu(OH) _{2} -silica tubes can be converted to any of the three copper oxide phases and to metallic copper, all in the tubular shape.
postsynthetic processing of silica tubes can be used to tune the composition, structure, and properties of the metal oxide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to produce and process a variety of Cu-based materials in a tubular form using a single synthetic procedure and postsynthetic processing.
the macroscopic tubularity of the samples is retained throughout the entire process.
it is possible to process materials with complex structures in a postsynthetic manner without destroying the macroscopic structure.
